title: AI-assisted literature mining of perovskite ink formulations using a hybrid regex-LLM extraction pipeline
content: Reproducibility of perovskite solar cell and LED fabrication depends critically on ink formulation details that are typically buried in the Methods sections of scientific articles. Manual curation of such data is slow, inconsistent, and does not scale. Here we present an end-to-end automated AI-assisted pipeline that (i) queries the OpenAlex academic graph to identify open-access publications containing perovskite ink formulations, (ii) downloads and parses PDF full texts using rule-based regex extraction, (iii) applies a large language model (LLM, Claude Haiku 4.5) as a second extraction layer to recover structured perovskite formulas, cleaned molarity values, and novel additive chemistries missed by regex, (iv) assigns a multi-criteria confidence score to each extracted recipe, and (v) exports a structured, analysis-ready dataset in tidy format. Applied to a corpus of 1041 screened publications, the pipeline recovered 68 annotated ink formulations from 71 successfully retrieved PDFs. The LLM extraction layer identified 46 structured perovskite formulas (31 unique compositions, including mixed-cation and quasi-2D types), increased molarity coverage from 49% to 60%, and increased high-confidence extractions from 32 (regex, score ≥7) to 36 (LLM confidence = high). Twenty records are automatically promoted and manually validated as the GOLD standard. The published data encompass 44 publication venues, and research articles published between 2014 and 2025, which record solvent systems, precursor stoichiometry, molarity, and additive solvent chemistry of halide perovskite inks. All code and data are freely available to accelerate materials informatics in this field.
